title: Re-Engineering of Rolling Stock with DC Motors as a Form of Sustainable Modernisation of Rail Transport in Eastern Europe After Entering EU in 2004 – Selected Examples and Problems Observed in Poland and Croatia with Some Perspectives for Ukraine
content: In 2004, the EU expanded with new central and Eastern European countries, including Poland. In 2013, Croatia entered the EU, while Ukraine 2022 became an official candidate to join the EU. In May 2024, the 20th Anniversary of Poland’s accession to the EU. In the first half of 2025, Poland took the presidency of the EU. It is worth presenting how, within these twenty years, the situation of rail rolling stock in railways and urban transport changed. Experience in the modernisation of old type of rail rolling stock with DC motors during a transition phase of railways with limited resources and long-term transformation of technology by local rolling stock companies in EU countries like Poland and Croatia. The paper briefly reviews the modernisation of DC-driven electric traction vehicles with examples of technical problems encountered in Poland and Croatia. The experience from Polish and Croatian cases may be useful for countries awaiting to join the EU, such as Ukraine, where the role of railway transport, still using mainly rolling stock with DC motors, is significant. Some concepts of modernisation of railway rolling stock in Ukraine are proposed and discussed.
